detail.longDescription: I have been trying to implement a randomized variant of Knuth's 1977 minimax algorithm for the 1971 board game "Mastermind". I know this is not at all unique but I thought it would be a good learning experience, and I wanted to make it able to be adaptable to different code lengths and colour options. Here is my code so far (written initially in Thonny and later in Spyder 6): import pickle from concurrent.futures import InterpreterPoolExecutor from itertools import combinations_with_replacement, product from os import cpu_count from random import choice, sample from statistics import mean, median from time import time with open("generated_resources/mark_guess_database.pickle", "rb") as mark_guess_database_file: mark_guess_database = pickle.load(mark_guess_database_file) del mark_guess_database_file pins_available_num = 6 code_len = 4 pin_options = tuple(range(1, pins_available_num + 1)) all_codes = tuple(product(pin_options, repeat=code_len)) all_clues = tuple( tuple(filter(bool, clue)) for clue in combinations_with_replacement((0, 1, 2), code_len) if clue != (1, 1, 1, 2) ) def create_solution(): return choice(all_codes) def mark_guess(guess, solution): return mark_guess_database[guess][solution] # helper logic for strategies def find_unguessed_codes(guess_board): return tuple(set(all_codes).difference(set(guess_board))) def find_consistent_codes(guess_board, clue_board, consistent_codes, num_to_check=1): guesses_to_check = guess_board[-num_to_check:] clues_to_check = clue_board[-num_to_check:] consistent_codes = list(consistent_codes) # finds all codes not ruled out by old guesses for guess, clue in zip(guesses_to_check, clues_to_check): for code in consistent_codes: if mark_guess(guess, code) != clue: consistent_codes.remove(code) return tuple(consistent_codes) def knuth_opening_46(): # knuth found this the best for a 4-6 game return tuple(sample(sample(pin_options, 2) * 2, 4)) def knuth_minimax(guess_board, clue_board, consistent_codes): minimax_codes = [None] minimax_value = 0 unguessed_codes = find_unguessed_codes(guess_board) for guess_candidate in unguessed_codes: min_eliminated = len(all_codes) + 1 for potential_clue in all_clues: eliminated = len(consistent_codes) - len( find_consistent_codes( guess_board + [guess_candidate], clue_board + [potential_clue], consistent_codes ) ) min_eliminated = min(eliminated, min_eliminated) if min_eliminated == minimax_value: minimax_codes.append(guess_candidate) elif min_eliminated > minimax_value: minimax_value = min_eliminated minimax_codes = [guess_candidate] consistent_minimax_codes = [] for code in minimax_codes: if code in consistent_codes: consistent_minimax_codes.append(code) if consistent_minimax_codes: return choice(consistent_minimax_codes) else: return choice(minimax_codes) # logic per strategy that decides on what functions to use when def knuth_algorithm(guess_board, clue_board, consistent_codes): consistent_codes = find_consistent_codes(guess_board, clue_board, consistent_codes) if len(guess_board) == 0: return knuth_opening_46(), consistent_codes return knuth_minimax(guess_board, clue_board, consistent_codes), consistent_codes # game logic, seperated due to potential concurrency def do_computer_game(strategy_function): guess_board = [] clue_board = [] solution = create_solution() guesses_this_game = 0 consistent_codes = all_codes[:] guess, consistent_codes = strategy_function(guess_board, clue_board, consistent_codes) guess_board.append(guess) clue_board.append(mark_guess(guess, solution)) consistent_codes = find_consistent_codes(guess_board, clue_board, consistent_codes) while guess_board[-1] != solution: guess, consistent_codes = strategy_function(guess_board, clue_board, consistent_codes) guess_board.append(guess) guesses_this_game += 1 clue_board.append(mark_guess(guess, solution)) return guesses_this_game # tests manager def do_computer_test(strategy_function, iterations, multithreaded): time_started = time() print("Started test.") strategy_functions = [strategy_function for i in range(iterations)] if multithreaded: with InterpreterPoolExecutor(max_workers=cpu_count()) as executor: game_results = tuple(executor.map(do_computer_game, strategy_functions)) else: game_results = tuple(map(do_computer_game, strategy_functions)) games = str(len(game_results)) maximum = str(max(game_results)) minimum = str(min(game_results)) meanavg = str(mean(game_results)) medianavg = str(int(median(game_results))) time_elapsed = round(time() - time_started, 3) time_elapsed_str = str(time_elapsed) time_per_game_ms = str(int(round(time_elapsed / iterations * 1000, 3))) multithreaded_str = str(multithreaded) print("\nFinished " + games + "-game test. Multithreaded: " + multithreaded_str + ".") print( "Time taken: " + time_elapsed_str + "s. Time per game on average: " + time_per_game_ms + "ms." ) print("Mean guesses: " + meanavg + ". Median guesses: " + medianavg + ".") print("Maximum guesses: " + maximum + ". Minimum guesses: " + minimum + ".") if __name__ == "__main__": do_computer_test(knuth_algorithm, 1, False) And here is the code that generates the mark_guess database: import pickle from itertools import product pins_available_num = 6 guess_len = 4 pin_options = tuple(range(1, pins_available_num+1)) all_codes = tuple(product(pin_options, repeat=guess_len)) def mark_guess(guess, solution): guess = list(guess) solution = list(solution) #lists have been copied to prevent global editing full_count = 0 #white pins half_count = 0 #black pins pin_index = 0 while pin_index != len(guess): if guess[pin_index] == solution[pin_index]: full_count += 1 solution.pop(pin_index) guess.pop(pin_index) #no pin_index += 1 here becuase a value was removed else: pin_index += 1 if len(guess) != 0: pin_index = 0 while pin_index != len(guess): if guess[pin_index] in solution: half_count += 1 solution.remove(guess[pin_index]) guess.pop(pin_index) else: pin_index += 1 return (*(1,) * full_count, *(2,) * half_count) print("Starting database generation.") mark_guess_database = dict.fromkeys(all_codes) for guess in all_codes: print(str(all_codes.index(guess) + 1) + " out of " + str(len(all_codes)), end="\r") mark_guess_database[guess] = {} for solution in all_codes: mark_guess_database[guess][solution] = mark_guess(guess, solution) print("\nFinished database generation. Dumping database to file.") with open("generated_resources/mark_guess_database.pickle", "wb") as mark_guess_database_file: pickle.dump(mark_guess_database, mark_guess_database_file) print("Done.") To my dismay, my implementation is terribly buggy, taking up to 10 guesses in some cases. I have no idea what I have done wrong. I would like to know whether anyone knows what part of my code isn't true to Knuth's algorithm (probably somewhere in the knuth_minimax function) and how I should change it. Thanks!
